subject: Exhibit D redlines: slab -> usage conversion + fallback proposal
messages:

Cc: contracts@acmepay.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit D redlines: pricing schedule and caps

Priyom —

Attached are ACME's redlines to Exhibit D. High-level items we marked: a hard cap on per-month spend for the first 12 months, a mandatory 'rebalancing' clause if monthly spend deviates >40% from the forecast for two consecutive months, and a preferred warranty that any slab->usage conversion preserves the customer's effective unit price (i.e., not materially increasing rates).

We also highlighted language around 'true-up' timing and the calculation base for the slab conversion. Legal wants confirmation you can (a) accept a temporary cap for onboarding and (b) propose fallback language for large spikes.

Attachment: ACME_Redline_ExhibitD.pdf (redline annotations)

Can you review and come back with Redwood's proposed edits? We have a procurement review on Friday and need to close the exhibit before then.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Procurement Ops
ACME Payments

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit D redlines: pricing schedule and caps

Team — forwarding ACME's redlines. Key asks summarized:
- Hard monthly cap for first 12 months (protects their P&L during onboarding)
- Rebalancing trigger at >40% deviation for 2 months
- Preservation of unit economics on slab->usage conversion
- Tight true-up timing and calculation base clarity

My proposal (high level):
- Accept a temporary onboarding cap but make it a soft cap with automatic downgrade to 'pay-as-used' after 3 overages in a 6-month window; keep overage pricing at published rates + small % uplift.
- For slab->usage conversion, include a conversion floor (so Redwood isn't forced below cost) and a one-time transition credit to ACME so their effective price doesn't spike immediately.
- Add an explicit spike-carveout: usage spikes >2x baseline for >7 consecutive days qualify for a surge protection clause (limited to 3 occurrences per contract year).

Marissa — can legal draft language for the soft cap + surge carveout that limits long-term liability? Ben — is a one-time transition credit (formula in attached pricing-matrix) ok from revenue ops perspective?

I attached a quick pricing matrix to illustrate the credit. Goal is to get to a redline we can send back today.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Att: pricing-matrix-illustration.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exhibit D redlines: pricing schedule and caps

Priyom / Ben —

Quick legal feedback and suggested guardrails:

1) Soft cap language: we can agree to a 'monthly onboarding cap' for the first twelve-month period, but it must be explicit that:
   - The cap is cumulative of billed usage (not an absolute entitlement).
   - Exceeding the cap triggers a 'cap remediation' path (automatic move to published pay-as-you-go rates for that month + documented overage notice).

2) Conversion floor & transition credit: we should include a formulaic floor: the per-unit price after conversion shall not be lower than 85% of the average per-unit rate billed during the prior three-month baseline period, unless otherwise agreed in writing. The one-time transition credit should be capped (e.g., no more than $X or Y% of first-year committed spend). That protects Redwood while addressing their 'preserve unit economics' ask.

3) Surge carveout: define a 'spike event' as >2.0x baseline for >7 consecutive days, capped to 3 occurrences per 12-month period. During a spike event we can apply temporary stabilization pricing; after 30 days of sustained spike, parties must reconcile via a true-up.

4) True-up timing: propose quarterly true-up windows; any retroactive adjustments limited to 90 days following the quarter close.

I'll prepare redline snippets for each of these bullets. Ben — confirm the cap on transition credit you can live with (suggested: lesser of $75k or 10% of first-year committed spend).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmepay.com>
Cc: contracts@acmepay.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exhibit D redlines: pricing schedule and caps

Alyssa —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear framing. We've discussed internally and attached a concise counterproposal (Redwood_Counter_ExhibitD_v2.pdf) that aims to balance ACME's onboarding protection needs with Redwood's economic guardrails. High-level summary of our counterterms:

- Onboarding cap: Redwood will accept a twelve-month onboarding cap, implemented as a "soft cap". A soft cap provides a billing cap but allows usage beyond the cap at published pay-as-you-go rates; after 3 months with overages in a rolling 6-month window, the account will shift to pay-as-you-go for the remainder of the onboarding period.

- Slab->Usage conversion: We propose a conversion floor set at 85% of the prior three-month average per-unit rate, plus a one-time transition credit (capped at the lesser of $75,000 or 10% of first-year committed spend) to smooth the customer's effective price impact.

- Spike/surge carveout: Define spike event >2x baseline for >7 consecutive days; spike protection available up to 3 events per 12-month period. Extended sustained spikes (>30 days) will trigger a true-up and potential temporary reprice.

- True-ups & timing: Quarterly true-ups with a 90-day lookback limit on any retro adjustments.

We believe these edits keep ACME protected in the critical onboarding window while capping Redwood's downside. If ACME can live with the capped transition credit, we should be able to finalize Exhibit D ahead of your procurement review Friday.

Attaching: Redwood_Counter_ExhibitD_v2.pdf (pdf) — redline snippets and clean copy. Also included pricing-matrix-illustration.xlsx to show the credit math.

If that's acceptable, I'll ask Legal to prepare the final track-changes for signature and route via DocuSign (linked: https://www.docusign.com/EXID/ACME-EXD-2025). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2025-07-45.

Best,
Priyom Das
